figure: Figure 6.2 — Latency distribution: the mean hides the tail
issue: Unexplained 0.01 s discrepancy in the stated mean between the figure legend and the facing-page prose. The §6.3.1 text (p.97) computes 'the two-point approximation of the mean is E[L] ≈ 0.99 × 0.8 + 0.01 × 5.0 ≈ 0.84 s', while the Fig 6.2 legend (p.98) prints 'mean = 0.85s'. The 0.85 s is the more accurate read-off sample mean (a log-normal with median 0.8 s and p95 ≈ 0.99 s has mean ≈ 0.807 s, so 0.99·0.807 + 0.01·5.0 ≈ 0.849 ≈ 0.85 s), but neither location says so. A reader comparing the two pages sees two different 'means' with no note that one is an approximation and the other the sample value.
evidence: p.97: '≈ 0.84 s — looks fine.' p.98 legend box: 'mean = 0.85s'. Recomputation: log-normal σ from p95/median = 0.99/0.8 = 1.2375 → σ ≈ 0.130 → log-normal mean ≈ 0.807 s; mixture mean = 0.99·0.807 + 0.01·5.0 ≈ 0.849 s ≈ 0.85 s, confirming the figure's value is the true sample mean and the text's 0.84 s is the crude two-point approximation.
acceptance_test: After the edit, the mean on p.97 and the mean in the Fig 6.2 legend are either identical or explicitly distinguished: e.g., the legend reads 'sample mean ≈ 0.85 s' and the prose adds a half-clause such as '(the read-off sample mean is ≈ 0.85 s; the 0.84 s above is the two-point approximation)'. A reader placing p.97 beside p.98 finds no unexplained 0.01 s difference in the stated mean.
